known_limitations: Upstream defines Sprintz-Delta and Sprintz-FIRE/XFF as distinct codec APIs; no predictor-neutral Sprintz bitstream/API exists, so the benchmark keeps two AlgorithmIDs.

Only lossless homogeneous 8/16-bit integer UTS and synchronous MTS with 1..128 dimensions are registered; float, lossy quantization, validity, asynchronous MTS and heterogeneous widths are unsupported.

The upstream 16-bit API reports length in int16_t units and cannot represent an odd final byte. The bounded wrapper independently parses the entire grammar and returns the exact validated byte length.

The immutable lzbench source closure is compiled through two replayed safety patches that fix unchecked allocations, leaks, low-dimensional overflow, generic 16-bit header overread, signed-shift UB and unsafe odd-dimension sizing.

ASan/UBSan qualification passes with -fno-sanitize=alignment because upstream deliberately uses packed unaligned x86 accesses; -fno-strict-aliasing is required. LeakSanitizer was not run because it is incompatible with the ptrace-managed host.
AVX2, BMI2 and LZCNT are mandatory; there is no scalar fallback, runtime dispatch or non-x86 portability claim.
One-shot single-thread operation only; streaming, query, random access and checksums are not registered.
Formal evidence uses one deterministic synthetic int16 MTS dataset and does not establish performance on real-world datasets. Failed diagnostic run sets remain append-only and are not reclassified.

The native binding files are now content-hashed in SourceArtifactID. An old compiled full-Sprintz wrapper rejected a valid 2048-element uint8 fixture although the current registered wrapper source accepts it. Rebuilt release/sanitizer artifacts replace it; upstream source and compression strategy are unchanged. Historical formal results are not current-source performance qualification.
